episode.title: Centralize hierarchical project trust before loading effect-bearing resources
episode.before: At parent 3d02d1da11ea4402f1a80c3df4df9fe57d53fe84, trust decisions were exact-directory lookups. The main runtime had its own trust resolver, while package commands used a separate simpler resolver that honored only an explicit override, absence of trust inputs, or an exact saved true decision; the config command defaulted to trusted. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md counted as trust-triggering inputs and were omitted when a project was untrusted. There was no global defaultProjectTrust policy, no parent-directory inheritance, and package/config commands did not run project_trust extension hooks.
episode.after: At d041b5cc354f9361207708395033e87cc78576cd, one resolver applies ordered trust sources across runtime, package, and config paths: explicit command override; automatic trust when no effect-bearing project inputs exist; a project_trust extension result loaded during an untrusted bootstrap pass; the nearest persisted directory decision; the global-only defaultProjectTrust policy; then an interactive prompt or fail-closed denial without UI. Persisted decisions can apply to a parent directory and be inherited by descendants, with child overrides removable. The resolved decision is installed into SettingsManager before project packages, extensions, skills, prompts, themes, system prompts, or local package-setting writes are processed. Passive AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md context remains readable regardless of trust and no longer triggers a trust prompt.
episode.diff: The merge adds core/project-trust.ts and reusable CLI trust/startup UI modules; extends the trust store with nearest-ancestor lookup, multi-path updates, parent-scope options, and inherited-decision metadata; adds a global-only defaultProjectTrust setting; extracts an untrusted extension bootstrap operation from ResourceLoader; routes normal runtime, package commands, and config commands through the same asynchronous trust resolver; preserves denial of trust-gated resources and local writes while removing context files from that gated set; and adds tests for precedence, extension hooks, inherited scopes, boundary classification, and non-interactive isolation.

evidence_units.claim: Pinned merge commit d041b5cc354f9361207708395033e87cc78576cd merged PR #5549 with subject 'feat(ui): Improved project approval settings' and first parent 3d02d1da11ea4402f1a80c3df4df9fe57d53fe84.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller --stat d041b5cc354f9361207708395033e87cc78576cd; issue-bundle.json resolved_commit and parent_commit

evidence_units.claim: The first-parent change adds project-trust policy and startup UI modules and modifies trust storage, resource loading, settings, package/config commands, interactive trust selection, and focused tests.

Before the change, ProjectTrustStore.get read only the normalized current-directory key, trust inputs included AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, package commands used an independent synchronous resolver, and config commands defaulted projectTrusted to true.

The centralized resolver evaluates explicit override first, returns trusted when no trust inputs exist, then consults project_trust extensions, persisted trust, global defaultProjectTrust, and finally UI; absence or cancellation of UI resolves to false.
Trust lookup walks from the normalized working directory toward the filesystem root and returns the nearest boolean decision; batched updates can set parent decisions and delete child overrides.
Trust-triggering inputs are limited to a local .pi directory or an ancestor .agents/skills directory; AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are not classified as trust inputs.

ResourceLoader performs a bootstrap pass with project trust forced false, reloads settings, and loads only the current non-project extension set before resolving trust; it then installs the decision, reloads settings, and resolves normal resources.

Package and config commands create SettingsManager as untrusted, optionally bootstrap project_trust extensions, call the centralized resolver with the global default, install the result, and reject local package-setting writes when untrusted.

The main runtime calls the centralized resolver from ResourceLoader.reload and supplies the command override, global default policy, bootstrap extension result, and a UI context whose availability depends on the active mode.

Trust-store tests prove nearest-parent inheritance, closest-child override precedence, removal of a child override to restore parent inheritance, and rejection of AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md as trust-triggering inputs.

Package-command tests prove that the global default can trust project packages, project_trust extensions can authorize package commands, and an explicit persisted false decision overrides a global always default.
Settings tests prove defaultProjectTrust is read only from global settings and invalid values fail safely to ask.
Resource-loader tests prove that an untrusted project still contributes AGENTS.md context while project system prompts, extensions, skills, prompts, and themes remain excluded.
A spawned-CLI test proves an untrusted non-interactive help invocation does not install project packages or emit their installation output.
Trust-selector tests prove inherited decisions are labeled with their source path and selecting parent trust produces a parent true update plus deletion of the current-directory override.

candidate_atomics.name: classify-trust-gated-project-effects
candidate_atomics.title: Separate passive project context from effect-bearing project resources
candidate_atomics.description: Define trust inputs around resources that can install packages, execute extensions, or alter runtime behavior, while allowing passive instruction files to remain available without forcing a trust decision.

semantic_action.intent: Avoid prompting for or denying trust merely because passive context exists, without exposing executable or configuration-driven project effects.
semantic_action.pre_state: Passive instruction files and effect-bearing project resources share one trust-triggering classification and are both suppressed when untrusted.
semantic_action.post_state: Only effect-bearing configuration and resource locations trigger trust resolution; passive context can load independently while executable and configuration resources remain gated.
semantic_action.validation: Create an untrusted project containing both instruction files and effect-bearing resources; assert instruction context loads, effect-bearing resources do not, and instruction files alone do not satisfy the trust-input predicate.

candidate_atomics.name: bootstrap-policy-hooks-under-denied-project-trust
candidate_atomics.title: Load policy hooks without activating project effects
candidate_atomics.description: Run a restricted bootstrap pass with project trust disabled so globally supplied or explicit hooks may decide trust before project-local packages and extensions become eligible.

semantic_action.intent: Allow extensible trust decisions without executing the untrusted project's own code during the decision process.
semantic_action.pre_state: Trust has not been resolved, but extension hooks may participate in the decision and normal loading could include project-local effects.
semantic_action.post_state: Decision hooks from non-project sources are available while project settings, packages, and extensions remain excluded until authorization completes.
semantic_action.validation: Provide a non-project project_trust hook and project package settings; verify the hook can authorize access and that the bootstrap loader begins with projectTrusted false.

candidate_atomics.name: resolve-layered-project-trust
candidate_atomics.title: Resolve authorization through one ordered fail-closed policy
candidate_atomics.description: Centralize trust resolution with explicit precedence across command overrides, absence of gated inputs, policy hooks, persisted decisions, global defaults, and interactive confirmation.

semantic_action.intent: Produce one consistent authorization result for every execution surface and deny unresolved effect-bearing projects in non-interactive contexts.
semantic_action.pre_state: Runtime and administrative commands may apply different trust rules, and no single precedence contract covers overrides, hooks, stored decisions, defaults, and UI availability.
semantic_action.post_state: All callers receive a boolean decision from the same precedence order, with persisted decisions overriding defaults and missing UI or cancelled prompts resolving to denial.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise explicit overrides, no-input projects, extension results, stored false over default always, valid and invalid global defaults, interactive selection, and headless fallback.

candidate_atomics.name: inherit-nearest-directory-authorization
candidate_atomics.title: Apply the closest saved authorization across directory scopes
candidate_atomics.description: Resolve persisted decisions hierarchically and update parent and child entries atomically so a parent policy can cover descendants without masking a closer exception.

semantic_action.intent: Support reusable authorization for a directory tree while retaining explicit, closer overrides and a way to resume inheritance.
semantic_action.pre_state: Persisted decisions apply only to an exact working directory, requiring duplicate entries and providing no inherited source metadata.
semantic_action.post_state: The nearest saved ancestor decision governs each descendant unless a closer decision exists; deleting the closer entry restores inheritance, and the effective source path is observable.
semantic_action.validation: Store a parent true decision, add a child false decision, query descendants, delete the child decision, and assert each effective value and source path.
parameters: nullable update used to delete an override

candidate_atomics.name: enforce-authorization-at-effect-boundaries
candidate_atomics.title: Install the decision before project effects and writes
candidate_atomics.description: Apply the resolved trust state to settings and resource resolution before loading project packages or resources, and reject project-local configuration writes when authorization is false.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent denied project configuration from causing package installation, code execution, runtime resource injection, or local settings mutation.
semantic_action.pre_state: A command is about to resolve project settings, install packages, load executable resources, or write project-local package configuration without a uniformly installed authorization result.
semantic_action.post_state: Denied projects contribute no gated resources or package-install effects and cannot receive local package-setting writes; authorized projects are reloaded and processed normally.
semantic_action.validation: For an untrusted project, assert project extensions, skills, prompts, themes, system prompt, and package installation output are absent and local configuration mutation is rejected; separately verify authorized package listing succeeds.

candidate_workflows.name: isolate-project-effects-behind-layered-authorization
candidate_workflows.title: Resolve project authorization before activating local effects
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for separating passive context from effect-bearing project inputs, safely loading non-project policy hooks, resolving one hierarchical authorization decision, and enforcing it across runtime and administrative command paths.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure project-local effects execute or mutate state only after one consistently resolved authorization decision, while passive context remains available and headless ambiguity fails closed.
when_to_use: A tool discovers project-local configuration, packages, plugins, scripts, skills, prompts, themes, or similar resources that can execute code or change runtime behavior.
Multiple entry points such as the main runtime, package commands, and configuration commands must share the same project authorization semantics.
Authorization may be supplied by explicit overrides, extension hooks, persisted directory policy, global defaults, or an interactive user decision.
anti_goals: Do not execute project-local hooks or install project packages to determine whether that same project is trusted.
Do not treat passive instruction files as equivalent to executable or configuration-driven effects unless repository evidence establishes that they execute effects.
Do not let a permissive default override an explicit persisted denial.
Do not silently authorize unresolved effect-bearing projects merely because the caller is non-interactive.
Do not require exact-directory duplication when an explicit parent-scope authorization is intended.
not_applicable_when: The project exposes no local input capable of executing code, installing dependencies, mutating configuration, or injecting runtime resources.
The caller has no project-local resource loading or mutation boundary to protect.
Authorization must not be inherited across directory ancestry for the target security model.
inputs: Canonical working directory and its ancestor chain
Inventory of passive context and effect-bearing project inputs
Explicit per-invocation authorization override, if present
Non-project policy-hook sources and hook result, if any
Resource loaders and project-local mutation operations to gate
workflow_graph.entry_state: Project trust is unresolved; project-local effect-bearing resources and settings must be considered unavailable, while non-project configuration is readable.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Exactly one authorization result has been installed before effect-bearing resolution: denied projects cannot load or mutate gated project state, authorized projects can be reloaded normally, passive context follows its separate classification, and any remembered scope is queryable with its source path.

steps.condition: Always, before deciding whether authorization is required.
steps.validation: The trust-input predicate is false for passive instruction files alone and true for the configured effect-bearing project markers.

steps.condition: Run only when no explicit override was supplied, gated inputs exist, and non-project policy hooks are supported.
steps.validation: Bootstrap settings report untrusted state and the loaded hook set excludes project-local packages and extensions.

steps.condition: Use when consulting or updating persisted authorization state.
steps.validation: Lookup returns the closest ancestor entry and deletion of a child entry restores the parent's effective decision.

steps.condition: Always when effect-bearing trust inputs exist; consume the bootstrap hook result when that optional step ran.
steps.validation: Precedence is override, hook, nearest persisted decision, global default, interactive decision, then denial; a stored false decision beats a global always default.

steps.condition: Before resolving project packages/resources or mutating project-local settings.
steps.validation: Denied execution exposes no gated project resources or install effects and refuses local writes; authorized execution reloads and exposes configured project resources.

validation_ladder: Unit-test the trust-input classifier, including passive-only and effect-bearing fixtures.
Unit-test hierarchical storage with parent inheritance, closer overrides, override deletion, malformed-store preservation, and source-path reporting.
Unit-test global default parsing and confirm project-local settings cannot set the default policy.
Integration-test decision precedence through package or resource call sites, including hook authorization and persisted denial over a permissive default.
Integration-test resource isolation so denied projects cannot supply executable/configuration resources while separately classified passive context remains available.
Spawn a non-interactive command and verify unresolved trust produces no project package-install side effects or structured-output contamination.
stop_conditions: Stop and deny project effects if trust remains unresolved and no interactive UI is available.
Stop and surface an error if the persisted trust store is malformed; do not overwrite it with a guessed decision.
Stop before project-local package installation, extension execution, or settings mutation if the resolved decision is false.
Defer hierarchical authorization if canonical ancestry or the intended inheritance boundary cannot be established safely.
unresolved_or_deferred: The available bundle contains no PR body, review discussion, or status-check results, so design intent beyond code, tests, and commit metadata is unavailable.
No test command was executed during this extraction; validation claims describe the checked-in test oracles at the pinned commit.

The change deliberately leaves passive project instructions outside the trust gate; whether instruction content itself should be treated as an effect in other systems is a project-specific policy decision, not established universally by this episode.

unresolved_questions: The issue bundle is a verified same-repository substitute for unresolved seed issue #9936, so this episode supports PR #5549 only and does not claim to resolve the seed issue's terminal-inheritance behavior.
Because GitHub discussion and CI metadata are unavailable, the evidence cannot establish which precedence choices were explicitly reviewed versus inferred from the merged implementation and tests.
